# E2E Test: Quantum Widget Decision

**Date:** 2026-04-01
**Participants:** Dave Quantum (VP Engineering)

Dave: "We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB for the analytics pipeline. 10x query performance, lower licensing cost."

Key decisions:
- **Database migration**: PostgreSQL → QuantumDB
- **Performance gain**: 10x analytical queries
- **Timeline**: Q3 2026

The map and index never vary with your focus; your per-call material is at the end.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

observations.why: Domain jargon (QuantumDB, analytics pipeline) used natively without glossing — the technical register the document's decision is performed in.
Flat, instrumental quantification of the benefit — no enthusiasm markers, just the number and the metric, performing a matter-of-fact register.
Bold heading with arrow notation and colon structure — a formal, document-structured register shift from the conversational source segments.
Same bold-heading, colon-delimited memo structure as src-3 — formal document register, consistent with the memo's structured summary section.
Bold-heading memo structure with calendar-quarter notation — formal document register, the third instance of this recurring structured-summary pattern.
First-person plural present continuous performs a settled course of action the speaker expects others to join — decision-grade ratification language, not a proposal being argued for.
Flat unhedged assertions presented as justification for the switch — asserted and ready to defend, but the segment offers evidence rather than performing the settling itself; claim, not decision.
The arrow notation records a settled transition as a performed declarative — the memo itself ratifies the migration as decided, not under discussion.
Restates the performance claim as a memo-recorded assertion; the memo reports the claim rather than performing the settling, and no ratification language is present.
A fixed timeline attached to the migration is an operational commitment — the speaker sets a date others are expected to plan around, which is decision-grade rather than a claim being argued.

positions.name: MigrationDecisionAcrossRegisters
positions.frame: How does the migration decision get carried from spoken declaration to memo record — what stays constant, and what shifts, across the register change?
positions.why: src-1 and src-3 assert the identical core content — the PostgreSQL-to-QuantumDB switch — as settled fact rather than as a proposal under discussion. The register dimension marks src-1 as conversational ('We're switching') and src-3 as formal memo notation ('→'), while the conviction dimension marks both as decision-grade rather than claim-grade: the memo does not argue the switch, it ratifies what the spoken segment already declared. Grouped as one accomplished decision restated across two document positions; held in tension only in how much formality/hedging each performs, not in what is being asserted.

positions.name: PerformanceCostJustificationAcrossRegisters
positions.frame: What quantified benefit is offered as justification for the migration, and how does that justification get restated from spoken claim to memo record?
positions.why: src-2 and src-4 both foreground the same '10x' performance multiple as the evidentiary basis for the switch. src-2 additionally names licensing cost, a dimension the memo excerpt (src-4) does not repeat — a genuine narrowing across the register shift, held here as tension rather than resolved. Conviction reads both as claim-grade (justification offered in support of a decision made elsewhere, not itself the settling act), and both relational/power reads mark the same market-pricing, rational-persuasion logic — quantified benefit as the ground for the decision — performed once conversationally and once in formal memo notation.

placements.why: The envelope's content is a technical infrastructure decision (a database platform migration for an analytics pipeline). No strata category exists yet in this repo, and nothing in the supplied taxonomy names technical/architecture decisions — the role description names Architecture as one of the org's canonical top-level strata, but it has not yet been minted here. This content is the first real call for it: a genuine organizational category (technical-system decisions), not a leaf-grain theme itself. Minted standalone per the NEW path — a strata mint needs no parent already in place.
placements.title: Technical system and infrastructure choices form their own organizational stratum
placements.frame: What technical architecture or infrastructure choice is being organized here?

placements.title: Infrastructure migrations are decided and scheduled on quantified performance-and-cost justification
placements.frame: What technical migration is being decided, what quantified benefit is offered to justify it, and what timeline is it committed to?
placements.why: The PostgreSQL-to-QuantumDB switch itself (src-1, src-3) is a one-time fact, not a theme in its own right — per the grain test, minting a leaf for that single event would be the failure mode the rule warns against. But the pattern it instantiates — a technical migration ratified as decided (not proposed), justified by a quantified performance/cost multiple (src-2, src-4), and pinned to a committed execution quarter (src-5) — is a subject future envelopes about other infrastructure decisions can keep feeding: the same shape (decision + quantified justification + timeline) recurs across an org's technical-change history. Grouped as one leaf rather than three because the position pass already shows these five segments as one continuous story carried across registers (spoken declaration restated as formal memo record) rather than independent themes; splitting them further would fragment weak, tightly-coupled support. Delivery dimensions (power's 'pressure' read on src-5, relational's 'authority-ranking' and 'market-pricing' reads) flagged the decision-making and justification patterns but explicitly route the topic here per this pass's ownership of content.
